milestone: PR9 default command-WAL public raw KV cutover
features: public Set/Delete/Batch.Write raw KV writes routed to RawKVBatch typed command frames
public command-WAL mode proof through treedb.write_path.mode=command_wal_cached
cached public command-WAL writes with the legacy cached redo journal disabled
physical backend flush batches that do not emit duplicate RawKVBatch command frames
checkpoint/close publication of covered command-WAL LSNs after cached flush
reopen from persisted command_wal_v1 with command_wal_cached mode proof
unified_bench public cached command-WAL variant for end-to-end batch-write comparison
local_validation_commands: GOWORK=off go run ./cmd/unified_bench -dbs treedb,treedb_public_command_wal -test batch_write -keys 200000 -batchsize 1024 -valsize 32 -profile wal_on_fast -treedb-maintenance-mode bench -treedb-command-wal-stats-scan -progress=false -format markdown

performance_gate.rationale: Public command-WAL writes now use the cached write path instead of direct backend root publication per point Set, and benchmark artifacts include explicit command_wal_cached mode proof. The short focused smoke is near parity for point Set and batch writes; the longer focused point Set run still shows a material typed-frame append/encode cost, and the end-to-end unified_bench public cached batch_write lane remains below legacy cached throughput. This is safe to review as performance evidence, but it should not be represented as strict throughput parity without an explicit accepted threshold or another optimization pass.

unsupported_modes: Update/UpdateSync remain rejected under cached public command-WAL until they have typed command coverage
DeleteRange remains rejected under cached public command-WAL until it has typed command coverage
next_required_work: optimize point Set command-frame encode/append overhead or establish an explicit accepted threshold before marking strict parity passed
optimize public command-WAL Batch.Write payload construction enough for unified_bench batch_write parity, or record an explicit accepted threshold and follow-up issue before default enablement
